items.text: SIX TRIALS, SIX DIFFERENT REGISTERED COMPOSITES. This is the widest endpoint divergence found in this programme, and every difference is stated in the trials' own registry records: SPRINT counts myocardial infarction, ACUTE CORONARY SYNDROME, stroke, HEART FAILURE and cardiovascular death -- five. ACCORD's blood-pressure trial counts NONFATAL myocardial infarction, NONFATAL stroke and cardiovascular death -- three, with no heart failure and no acute coronary syndrome. BPROAD counts four. ESPRIT counts five INCLUDING CORONARY OR NON-CORONARY REVASCULARISATION. STEP counts SIX, and one of them is ATRIAL FIBRILLATION, which appears in no other trial on this page. AND SPS3 IS NOT A COMPOSITE TRIAL AT ALL. Its registration declares TWO separate primary outcomes, each a single event type -- 'clinically defined ischemic stroke' and 'hemorrhagic stroke'. It counts stroke recurrence and nothing else. A stroke-only endpoint cannot be averaged into a five- or six-component cardiovascular composite. SEPARATELY: THE PAGE CANNOT AGREE WITH ITSELF ABOUT HOW MANY TRIALS THIS IS. Its include list names SIX registrations. Its embedded data carries ONE -- SPRINT. The index card published k=5. Three different counts, and no surface reconciles them. SEPARATELY AGAIN: THE PUBLISHED NUMBER CANNOT COME FROM THIS PAGE. HR 0.79 (0.71 to 0.87) is a five-trial pool, and the page holds an effect for exactly one trial. It also matches neither published benchmark this page carries.

[P38] The reading holds 3 DIFFERENT COMPARATOR FAMILIES: LMWH_OR_HEPARIN, OTHER_DOAC, PLACEBO. A shared estimand would not make these poolable -- the contrast differs, not just the measurement. [P37] 6 DISTINCT registered-primary titles across 7 trials. Compared on their verbatim text, not on the word 'composite'.

The four trials surfaced by the strategy question register FOUR DIFFERENT primary composites, differing at the component level: CASTLE-AF and RAFT-AF count all-cause death plus heart-failure events; CABANA counts total mortality, disabling stroke, serious bleeding and cardiac arrest; EAST-AFNET 4 counts CARDIOVASCULAR death, stroke and hospitalisation. One counts all-cause death, another counts cardiovascular death, and two count event classes the others do not. The withholding question was asked at every registered rank and found no shared estimand, because RAFT-AF registers no secondary outcome at all.

FIDAXOMICIN IS THE COMPARATOR IN ALL THREE TRIALS AND EXPERIMENTAL IN NONE. Recurrence is shared at some rank across all three, so the OUTCOME limb passes -- AND THE TOPIC STILL CLOSES, because a page titled for a drug that is the control arm everywhere is not asking the question its title asks. Fourth instance of the comparator-as-subject shape. AUTHORITY: MECIR Box 10.10.a C62 -- 'Undertake (or display) a meta-analysis only if participants, interventions, comparisons and outcomes are judged to be sufficiently similar to ensure an answer that is clinically meaningful.'

EIGHT TRIALS ARE ELIGIBLE AND NOT ONE HAS POSTED A RESULT. Sarcoidosis, interstitial lung disease, diastolic heart failure, sickle-cell disease twice, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, and a treatment-regimen comparison. Six of the eight register a walk-distance endpoint and three a clinical-worsening outcome, SO THE SHARED ESTIMAND EXISTS ON PAPER AND IN NO DATABASE. Two are TERMINATED at n=14 and n=12 and one was WITHDRAWN at n=0.

Only one staged source prints an extractable between-arm difference for this endpoint, and that -- not the form of the quantity -- is why nothing is pooled. A mean difference in metres on a common scale is poolable by generic inverse variance like any other, so a later lane that obtains the full texts of the other trials registering a walk-distance endpoint could pool this estimand properly. An earlier version of this field said the FORM would prevent it, which is stricter than the Handbook, false of a mean difference, and contradicted by this object's own handbook block three fields away.

THIS PAGE SEEDS NO REGISTRATION AT ALL. There is nothing to read, nothing to pool and nothing to withhold. Not a judgement about caspofungin: a statement that this page carries no trial identity. AUTHORITY: MECIR Box 10.10.a C62 -- 'Undertake (or display) a meta-analysis only if participants, interventions, comparisons and outcomes are judged to be sufficiently similar to ensure an answer that is clinically meaningful.'

THREE TRIALS, THREE INFECTIONS, THREE PRIMARIES: complicated urinary tract infection with pyelonephritis, complicated intra-abdominal infection, and hospital-acquired or ventilator-associated pneumonia whose primary is ALL-CAUSE MORTALITY. No outcome concept is common to all three at ANY rank once adverse events are set aside. AUTHORITY: MECIR Box 10.10.a C62 -- 'Undertake (or display) a meta-analysis only if participants, interventions, comparisons and outcomes are judged to be sufficiently similar to ensure an answer that is clinically meaningful.'

THE THREE TRIALS DO NOT SHARE ONE ENDPOINT DEFINITION, and each registry record says so in its own words. All three composites count kidney-function decline, but at three different thresholds: CREDENCE counts a DOUBLING OF SERUM CREATININE, DAPA-CKD counts a SUSTAINED DECLINE OF AT LEAST 50 PER CENT IN eGFR, and EMPA-KIDNEY counts a SUSTAINED DECLINE OF AT LEAST 40 PER CENT IN eGFR. Those are three different events, and the decline component is the largest contributor to each composite: a 40 per cent threshold admits strictly more patients than a 50 per cent threshold, which admits strictly more than a doubling of creatinine. The end-stage component differs too -- CREDENCE and DAPA-CKD floor it at an eGFR below 15, EMPA-KIDNEY at an eGFR below 10. SEPARATELY AND SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN: every per-trial value this review held was an ODDS RATIO DERIVED BY US from 2x2 counts, while all three trials analyse TIME TO FIRST OCCURRENCE -- DAPA-CKD's registry record states that 'the proportional hazards Cox regression model takes into account the time to the event'. The index card published that derived odds ratio under the label HR.

THE PUBLISHED ESTIMATE IS THE COMPARATOR, NOT THE FINDING. The index card served 'Published: HR 0.81 (0.73 to 0.91), k=4'. This page's own bytes embed PUBLISHED_META_BENCHMARKS = Ruff 2014, 'Ruff pooled DOAC vs warfarin MA (stroke/SE)', measure RR, estimate .81, lci .73, uci .91, k 4, Lancet 2014;383:955-962 -- a locked local database of published syntheses this review is meant to be COMPARED AGAINST. All four numbers on the card are those four numbers. This object's own pooled value is OR 0.7817 (0.6710 to 0.9108) at k=3 and shares no digit with the card. The one place the page held a correct external value is the value that migrated into the claim position, and the measure was relabelled from RR to HR on the way. SEPARATELY AND SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN: k IS OVERSTATED. The card and the page's AUTO_INCLUDE_TRIAL_IDS both say four trials; three are pooled. ROCKET AF carries no event counts on the page, so a pool derived from 2x2 counts drops it in silence, and it is the trial whose registered result is closest to no effect. SEPARATELY AGAIN: THE MEASURE IS MISNAMED. Every per-trial value here is an ODDS RATIO THIS PROJECT DERIVED from 2x2 counts -- the object says so in its own derivation_note -- while all four registry records register a Cox proportional-hazards analysis of TIME TO FIRST EVENT and report a hazard ratio. A derived odds ratio was published under the label HR.

THE TRIALS DO NOT SHARE ONE ENDPOINT, AND ONE WHOLE COMPONENT IS PRESENT IN ONE AND ABSENT FROM THE OTHERS. COLCOT's registered primary, verbatim, is 'First Event of Cardiovascular Death, RESUSCITATED CARDIAC ARREST, Acute Myocardial Infarction, Stroke, or URGENT HOSPITALIZATION FOR ANGINA REQUIRING CORONARY REVASCULARIZATION' -- five components. CLEAR SYNERGY's colchicine primary is 'Composite of cardiovascular death, recurrent myocardial infarction, stroke, or unplanned ischemia driven revascularization' -- four, with NO cardiac-arrest component and a different revascularisation trigger. LoDoCo2's, per this page's own benchmark record, is CV death, SPONTANEOUS myocardial infarction, ischaemic stroke, or ischaemia-driven coronary revascularisation. AND CONVINCE IS NOT A COMPOSITE TRIAL AT ALL. Its registration declares THREE SEPARATE PRIMARY OUTCOMES -- 'Recurrence of non-fatal ischemic stroke', 'non-fatal Major Cardiac event', and 'Vascular death' -- and the first of them counts RECURRENT NON-FATAL ISCHAEMIC STROKE AND NOTHING ELSE. A single-component stroke-recurrence outcome cannot be averaged with a five-component cardiovascular composite. SEPARATELY: THE PAGE CANNOT AGREE WITH ITSELF ABOUT HOW MANY TRIALS THIS IS. Its AUTO_INCLUDE_TRIAL_IDS names FIVE -- COLCOT, LoDoCo2, COPS, CLEAR SYNERGY and CONVINCE. Its embedded trial data carries THREE. The index card published k=2. Three different counts on one page, and nothing reconciles them. SEPARATELY AGAIN: THE PUBLISHED NUMBER IS NOT RECONSTRUCTABLE. The card served 'HR 0.75 (0.61 to 0.91), k=2'. Thirty-three candidate pools were computed from this page's own four published hazard ratios -- every subset of two, three and four trials, under fixed-effect, DerSimonian-Laird and REML -- and NONE gives 0.75 (0.61 to 0.91). The closest, LoDoCo2 with CONVINCE under DerSimonian-Laird, gives 0.755 (0.623 to 0.915). Search bounded at 33 pools and reported as bounded. AND WHICHEVER TWO TRIALS IT WAS, THE POOL EXCLUDES CLEAR SYNERGY IN SILENCE -- the largest trial here at 7,264 randomised, and the only one whose result is null at 0.99 (0.85 to 1.16). Nothing on the page states that it was left out.

TWO OF THE THREE TRIALS ON THIS PAGE REGISTER ONLY CONTINUOUS PRIMARY OUTCOMES, AND THIS PAGE POOLED EVENT COUNTS. Verbatim: STEP-HFpEF and STEP-HFpEF DM each register two co-primaries, 'Change in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score' and 'Change in Body Weight'. Both are CONTINUOUS CHANGE SCORES. Neither is an event count and neither can produce a 2x2 table. The counts stored for STEP-HFpEF DM, 7 of 310 against 18 of 306, CORRESPOND TO NO REGISTERED PRIMARY OUTCOME OF THAT TRIAL. SUMMIT is different and is the only row here with a defensible source: it registers a continuous KCCQ primary AND 'First Occurrence of the Composite Endpoint of Heart Failure (HF) Outcomes', and its stored 29 of 364 against 52 of 367 do correspond to that event co-primary. So the pool joins one trial's registered event composite to another trial's unregistered counts. SEPARATELY: THE OUTCOME NAME AND THE MEASURE DESCRIBE DIFFERENT QUANTITIES. The outcome is named 'Change in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score' and the stored measure is an ODDS RATIO. A change score has no odds. SEPARATELY AGAIN, AND IT IS WHY THIS TOPIC WAS INVISIBLE: THIS PAGE HAD NO INDEX CARD AT ALL. It is linked from the index table and appears in no card, so it published a pooled odds ratio of 0.4846 (0.3178 to 0.7389) that the corpus's own card-alignment checking could never reach -- there was no card to compare against the page.

THE PUBLISHED VALUES APPEAR IN NEITHER TRIAL'S SOURCE RECORD, AND THE ARMS PAIRED TO PRODUCE THEM ARE A COMPARISON NEITHER TRIAL PERFORMED. BOTH TRIALS ARE FOUR-ARM 2x2 DESIGNS of dosing frequency, and each registers TWO treatment comparisons, both WITHIN a frequency. BERSON registers Placebo Q2W against Evolocumab Q2W, -70.29 (-75.43 to -65.16), and Placebo QM against Evolocumab QM, -70.04 (-74.67 to -65.41). Hua Tuo registers Placebo Q2W against Evolocumab 140 mg Q2W, -70.73 (-77.98 to -63.48), and Placebo QM against Evolocumab 420 mg QM, -69.74 (-76.51 to -62.97). THIS OBJECT CROSSES THE FREQUENCIES ON BOTH TRIALS: it pairs BERSON's placebo Q2W arm with its MONTHLY evolocumab arm, and Hua Tuo's placebo Q2W arm with its MONTHLY 420 mg arm. Neither cross-pairing was registered, analysed or reported by anyone. AND THE STORED VALUES MATCH NOTHING. BERSON is held here as -71.8 (-81.39 to -62.21) against registered values of -70.29 and -70.04; Hua Tuo as -70.8 (-80.57 to -61.03) against -70.73 and -69.74. Neither stored value is either registered comparison, and neither is the difference between ANY two of the four arm means each trial reports. The stored intervals are roughly half again as wide as the registered ones. SEPARATELY: THE ARM ROLES ARE INVERTED ON BOTH TRIALS. The arm carrying role TREATMENT is the placebo arm on Hua Tuo ('Placebo Q2W') and the statin-only arm on BERSON ('Atorvastatin (Q2W)'), while the evolocumab arm carries role CONTROL on both. This is the fourth object in which that inversion has been found and the first in which the arms were ALSO cross-paired.
Only one independent cohort reports this estimand over this window, so there is nothing to combine. That is a limit of the evidence, not a choice made here.

Nothing is pooled: one trial. This is not a withheld estimate -- the value stands and is CLEAR Outcomes' own.

THE FOUR TRIALS DO NOT ANSWER ONE QUESTION, AND ONE OF THEM DOES NOT MEASURE AN ISCHAEMIC EVENT AT ALL. This estimate averaged four different comparisons into a single pairwise odds ratio. (1) THE CONTRASTS DIFFER: PLATO is ticagrelor against clopidogrel; TRITON-TIMI 38 is prasugrel against clopidogrel; ISAR-REACT 5 is ticagrelor against prasugrel; TWILIGHT is ticagrelor plus aspirin against ticagrelor alone, which is an aspirin-withdrawal question and not a P2Y12 comparison. Four contrasts over three drugs plus an aspirin question is a NETWORK, and a network cannot be reduced to one pairwise pool. (2) TWILIGHT CONTRIBUTES A BLEEDING ENDPOINT. Its registered primary, verbatim, is 'Number of Participants With BARC Type 2, 3, or 5' -- described as 'first occurrence of clinically relevant bleeding episode'. It is the trial's ONLY registered primary. A harm endpoint was averaged with three efficacy composites, which is the same defect this corpus withdrew DOAC_CANCER_VTE and APIXABAN_ACS for. (3) THE THREE ISCHAEMIC COMPOSITES ARE NOT IDENTICAL EITHER: PLATO counts 'Death From Vascular Causes, Myocardial Infarction (MI), and Stroke' to 12 months; TRITON counts 'Cardiovascular (CV) Death, Nonfatal Myocardial Infarction (MI), or Nonfatal Stroke' to 15 months -- a different death term, NONFATAL restrictions the others do not carry, and a window three months longer; ISAR-REACT 5 counts 'Composite of death, myocardial infarction or stroke' to 12 months, where 'death' is unqualified and therefore all-cause. Three death definitions across three trials. (4) THE HETEROGENEITY ALREADY SAID SO: I-squared 91.0%, Q 33.4 on 3 degrees of freedom, and the per-trial estimates run from 0.55 to 1.37 -- ISAR-REACT 5 points the opposite way to the rest. Withdrawn: the displayed value 0.8371 (0.6576-1.0657) is not an estimate of anything one question could ask.

[P38] The reading holds 2 DIFFERENT COMPARATOR FAMILIES: OTHER_DOAC, VKA. A shared estimand would not make these poolable -- the contrast differs, not just the measurement. [P37] 4 DISTINCT registered-primary titles across 5 trials. Compared on their verbatim text, not on the word 'composite'.
Only one independent cohort reports this estimand over this window, so there is nothing to combine. That is a limit of the evidence, not a choice made here.

TWO TRIALS IN DIFFERENT INFECTIONS -- complicated INTRA-ABDOMINAL infection against complicated URINARY TRACT infection -- and BOTH register ADVERSE-EVENT counts as their primary rather than efficacy. Clinical cure and microbiological eradication appear at some rank in both, and A SHARED CONCEPT ACROSS DIFFERENT DISEASES IS NOT A SHARED QUANTITY: cure of an abdominal infection and cure of a urinary infection are the same words about different events. AUTHORITY: MECIR Box 10.10.a C62 -- 'Undertake (or display) a meta-analysis only if participants, interventions, comparisons and outcomes are judged to be sufficiently similar to ensure an answer that is clinically meaningful.'

[P45] 1 trial(s) register a primary that fuses a THROMBOTIC and a BLEEDING component in one endpoint. That measures neither efficacy nor safety, so it cannot join either. TWO TRIALS OF LYMPHATIC FILARIASIS, measuring microfilarial clearance, AND ONE OF MALARIA, measuring clinical malaria episodes. Two different diseases under one heading. No outcome concept is common to all three at any rank. AUTHORITY: MECIR Box 10.10.a C62 -- 'Undertake (or display) a meta-analysis only if participants, interventions, comparisons and outcomes are judged to be sufficiently similar to ensure an answer that is clinically meaningful.'

[P38] The reading holds 2 DIFFERENT COMPARATOR FAMILIES: PLACEBO, VKA. A shared estimand would not make these poolable -- the contrast differs, not just the measurement. [P37] 2 DISTINCT registered-primary titles across 2 trials. Compared on their verbatim text, not on the word 'composite'.

THREE TRIALS WITH THREE DIFFERENT PRIMARIES: emergence of resistance, all-cause mortality at day 28, and all-cause mortality at day 14. Clinical cure appears at some rank in all three, but the trials span bacterial pneumonia, carbapenem-resistant bloodstream infection and hospital-acquired pneumonia -- and two different mortality WINDOWS are two different quantities. AUTHORITY: MECIR Box 10.10.a C62 -- 'Undertake (or display) a meta-analysis only if participants, interventions, comparisons and outcomes are judged to be sufficiently similar to ensure an answer that is clinically meaningful.'

The four trials do not share one endpoint. DAPA-HF and DELIVER count cardiovascular death, hospitalisation for heart failure, OR AN URGENT HEART-FAILURE VISIT; EMPEROR-Reduced and EMPEROR-Preserved count cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure only. Two trials count an event class the other two do not, so this pool combined quantities that are not the same quantity. Verified word for word against each trial's registry entry rather than assumed.
Only one independent cohort reports this estimand over this window, so there is nothing to combine. That is a limit of the evidence, not a choice made here.

TWO TRIALS OF COMPLICATED URINARY TRACT INFECTION with microbiological eradication primaries, AND ONE OF BLOODSTREAM INFECTION due to carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae whose primary is ALL-CAUSE MORTALITY. Clinical cure appears at some rank in all three; a urinary infection and a bloodstream infection are not one population. AUTHORITY: MECIR Box 10.10.a C62 -- 'Undertake (or display) a meta-analysis only if participants, interventions, comparisons and outcomes are judged to be sufficiently similar to ensure an answer that is clinically meaningful.'

THE ENDPOINTS AGREE AND THE MEASURE IS THE DEFECT -- WHICH MAKES THIS THE OPPOSITE OF EVERY OTHER TOPIC IN THIS PASS. All three registrations read declare the same primary, verbatim: 'Percent Change From Baseline in Fasting Low Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol (LDL-C) at Week 12'. THAT IS A CONTINUOUS QUANTITY. IT HAS NO EVENTS. An odds ratio requires a 2x2 table of participants who did and did not experience something, and a percent change in a laboratory value produces no such table. This page derived one anyway. WHAT THE COUNTS ACTUALLY ARE IS NOT RECORDED, AND THEIR MAGNITUDE SHOWS THEY ARE NOT EVENTS: SPIRE-LDL is stored as 971 in 1,068 placebo participants -- 91 per cent -- which is a threshold or responder flag of some kind, applied to an endpoint whose registered form is a mean change. Deriving an odds ratio from an undocumented dichotomisation of a continuous outcome discards the effect size the trials were designed to estimate and replaces it with a quantity that depends entirely on where the unrecorded threshold was placed.
no shared estimand -- see poolable_reason

[P38] The reading holds 2 DIFFERENT COMPARATOR FAMILIES: PLACEBO, USUAL_CARE_OR_NO_TREATMENT. A shared estimand would not make these poolable. [P37] 24 DISTINCT registered-primary titles across 26 trials, compared on their verbatim text.

Only one contributing trial reports this estimand, and the FORM of the quantity would prevent pooling even if a second did: it counts PAIRS rather than participants or events, its direction of benefit is inverted relative to every other ratio here, and its interval is not at the level the others use.
Each retained trial contributes counts for this outcome. Numbers sufficient to do the arithmetic are a prerequisite for pooling, not a justification for it; see the interpretation caveat.

TWO TRIALS IN DIFFERENT INFECTIONS: URINARY TRACT infection with a MICROBIOLOGICAL primary against complicated INTRA-ABDOMINAL infection with a CLINICAL one. Both concepts appear at some rank in both trials, and the populations still differ -- the participants limb fails and no outcome repairs it. AUTHORITY: MECIR Box 10.10.a C62 -- 'Undertake (or display) a meta-analysis only if participants, interventions, comparisons and outcomes are judged to be sufficiently similar to ensure an answer that is clinically meaningful.'

THREE TRIALS, THREE UNRELATED REGISTERED PRIMARIES. Verbatim: EXPLORER-HCM registers a composite responder definition built from peak oxygen consumption and NYHA class. VALOR-HCM registers a 'Composite of Decision to Proceed With Septal Reduction Therapy (SRT) and SRT Guideline Eligible at Week 16' -- A TREATMENT-DECISION ENDPOINT, which measures what clinicians decided rather than what happened to patients. The Chinese phase 3 registers 'Change From Baseline to Week 30 in Valsalva Left Ventricular Outflow Tract (LVOT) Peak Gradient' -- A CONTINUOUS HAEMODYNAMIC MEASUREMENT with no events at all. A responder proportion, a decision, and a pressure gradient are three different kinds of quantity, and no single odds ratio can carry them. THE ORIGINAL WITHDRAWAL REASON WAS A NUMERIC ONE AND IT IS RETAINED BELOW, BUT IT WAS NOT THE DEEPEST FAULT: the page's stated ground was that a value of 6.67 implied a much smaller table than these arms. That is true and it is a symptom. The cause is that only ONE of the three trials has any counts on this page at all, and the other two register endpoints that could not have produced counts to begin with.
Only one independent cohort reports this estimand over this window, so there is nothing to combine. That is a limit of the evidence, not a choice made here.

BOTH TRIALS REGISTER HIERARCHICAL ENDPOINTS ANALYSED BY WIN RATIO, AND A WIN RATIO CANNOT BE RECOVERED FROM A 2x2 TABLE. ATTR-ACT's registered primary, verbatim, is a 'Hierarchical Combination of All-Cause Mortality and Frequency of Cardiovascular-Related Hospitalizations'. In such an analysis every patient in one arm is compared with every patient in the other and the result is a ratio of wins to losses; there is no numerator over a denominator to extract, and reducing it to counts of participants discards the hierarchy that defines it. AND THE TWO HIERARCHIES ARE NOT THE SAME HIERARCHY. ATTRibute-CM's registered primary is a 'Hierarchical Combination of All-Cause Mortality, Cumulative Frequency of CV-related Hospitalization, CHANGE FROM BASELINE IN NT-proBNP and CHANGE FROM BASELINE IN 6MWT'. That is FOUR levels to ATTR-ACT's two, and its lower two levels are CONTINUOUS CHANGE SCORES rather than events. Two hierarchies of different depth, whose tie-breaking rules differ and whose lower levels are not even the same kind of quantity, do not estimate one thing.
Only one independent cohort reports this estimand over this window, so there is nothing to combine. That is a limit of the evidence, not a choice made here.
